Date: MARCH 11, 1996

Subject: • PM INSTITUTE--OPERATING AND INTERNAL ACCOUNTING CONTROLS

The following summarizes my concerns surrounding the Institute's control environment. As you and I have discussed many times in the past, I believe the controls are very weak in a number of areas of the PM Institute.

During a meeting on August 1, 1995, with Dr. Brenner and Kevin Sweeney from Shook, Hardy & Bacon L.L.P. (S,H&B), I distributed the attached control summary outlining the initiation of the implementation of minimum controls for the Institute. To my knowledge the only controls that have been implemented to date are those which my staff and I have established at MVC for the control of the Institute's assets. I realize that the Institute has been in a state of flux since the employees originally targeted to start up this venture have not accepted employment with the Institute. S,H&B has no doubt been kept busy with alternative structures for the organization in an effort to attract world renown scientists.

The fact remains that the Institute and PM in particular, could have potential exposure in a number of areas. Listed below is a summary of the issues I believe should be improved by the implementation of internal controls and operating procedures.

• The lack of supervision for the current employees is a key control missing at the Institute at this time. Without any supervision a whole range of issues are of concern. Some of the more significant areas of concern would be appropriateness of the scientific research, disposal of toxic waste, conformance to Federal and State safety regulations, and appropriateness of the purchases of goods and services received.
